issue: The audited build is NOT the build customers see. Production www.padmashreetravels.in serves an older build than the preview.
evidence: Investigated 12 Sep 2026. Both hosts are Vercel (Server: Vercel, region bom1). Production landing.css sha 531c725a09a4 matches NO commit in either git history (30 most recent commits touching that file scanned in both). Preview sha e38fad602246 == origin/master (23be435). Production homepage lacks: conversion-tracking.js, premium review variant, collapsible SEO block, teal section system, footer wordmark; and still contains the retired "Verified reviews on Google" band.
affected visitor: All visitors on the real domain
likely booking impact: Every fix in this report stays invisible to customers until production is redeployed.
recommendation: See UX-IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT.md section 4 for the full deployment recommendation and rollback. Requires Vercel dashboard access to confirm which project holds the www domain.
acceptance criteria: curl of css/landing.css returns an identical sha256 on www.padmashreetravels.in and the preview URL.
resolution_note: Investigated, not actionable from the repository alone. Domain-to-project assignment cannot be read from local config.

Higher specificity replaced the background but not the colour. Measured 1.07:1 across 37 rendered th elements.
affected visitor: Anyone reading a blog itinerary or fare table
likely booking impact: Unreadable fare/itinerary tables undermined the fare-transparency message.
recommendation: Removed the accidental background/font overrides from the Jul-2026 scroll fix so the original dark-header design in blog.css applies.
acceptance criteria: Computed contrast >= 4.5:1 on all 12 articles at all four viewports.
resolution_note: FIXED. css/style.css:2176 now sets only white-space:nowrap. Measured 1.07:1 -> 19.8:1 on 37 th elements, 0 articles failing, at 360/390/768/1440. .ftbl unaffected (19.24:1). Scroll wrapper retained (overflow-x:auto). Before/after screenshots in audit/screenshots/.

issue: Cancellation and refund terms appear on 3 of 59 pages (5%); payment methods on 11 (19%).
evidence: Topic scan across 59 public pages. Additional context found during implementation: docs/claims-policy-audit.md shows the cancellation policy was DELIBERATELY removed from metadata, schema and visible text because it could not be evidenced. The sparseness is an existing owner-approved decision, not an oversight.
likely booking impact: Cancellation and payment ambiguity is a pre-enquiry drop-off point.
recommendation: Publish one canonical Booking Terms block once the owner confirms the real policy. Do not restore the previous wording without confirmation.
acceptance criteria: A single terms source is linked from /book/, /agra-taxi-fares/ and every route page.
resolution_note: Cancellation OWNER-CONFIRMED 2026-09-12: free at least 12 hours before departure. Published on book/, agra-to-sirsaganj/, the homepage FAQ (visible + FAQPage schema) and under the final CTA on 36 route pages = 38 pages. A stale maintainer note citing the old 2-hour figure was resolved on both pages it named. Late-cancellation charges, no-show terms and advance-refund handling remain UNCONFIRMED and are stated nowhere. PAYMENT METHODS still pending owner (Q7).

URL/template: Whole site (57 pages carry the dominant phrasing)
issue: "Available 24/7" is asserted site-wide with no stated basis.
evidence: Claim catalogue built during implementation: 38 distinct phrasings. Dominant: "Available 24/7." on 57 pages (footer brand line). Others include "We run 24 hours a day, every day of the year including holidays and festivals." (4 pages, visible + schema) and "Available 24 hours a day, with same-day booking usually possible." (2 pages, schema). Not covered by the earlier claims audit, so this is a new finding.
affected visitor: All visitors, especially airport and sunrise journeys
likely booking impact: Availability is the load-bearing promise for those journeys.
recommendation: Confirm what is genuinely guaranteed, then either keep or replace with: "Call or message us to check availability for your travel time — we confirm before you book."
acceptance criteria: Every instance is owner-confirmed or uses the softened wording, including the schema copies.
resolution_note: OWNER-CONFIRMED 2026-09-12: support runs daily 9 AM-9 PM IST. Implemented site-wide. Claims were classified before editing into SUPPORT (6 phrasings, 57 pages - replaced with the confirmed hours), OPERATIONS (17 phrasings - de-absolutised to on-request wording, so the site neither promises round-the-clock pickups nor claims they stop at 9 PM) and AMBIGUOUS (17 phrasings - classified individually by rendered context). Verified: 0 rendered availability absolutes across all 59 public pages; 12 remain only inside HTML editorial comments and are flagged, not changed. Vehicle/pickup hours remain UNCONFIRMED.

issue: Homepage transfers ~1.6 MB, of which ~1.55 MB is imagery, with no responsive images.
evidence: Live measurement: 1603 KB total, 1546 KB images, 23 requests. 13 image files; 12 destination cards 65-184 KB each. srcset on 0 of 15 ; no preload. TTFB median 195 ms — the weight is payload, not latency. 13 of 15 images already carry loading=lazy.
affected visitor: Journey F — in-market visitor on a slow mobile connection
likely booking impact: Highest-intent journey served the heaviest page.
recommendation: Generate width-variant derivatives and add srcset/sizes to the destination cards.
acceptance criteria: Homepage image transfer at 390px is under 600 KB.
resolution_note: DEFERRED. The meaningful win (srcset) requires generating new image derivatives, which is an asset-production task rather than a code fix, and would add ~36 binary files. Flagged for a dedicated pass so it can be reviewed as an asset change.

issue: Heading levels were skipped, breaking the document outline.
evidence: Reproduced: 26 skips across 20 pages. Two dominant patterns — h2 -> h4 (legacy footer column headings and blog card/timeline titles) and h1 -> h3 (3 pages).
likely booking impact: A broken outline hides content from heading-based navigation.
recommendation: Re-sequence heading levels; update the three element-in-selector CSS rules in the same pass so styling is unchanged.
acceptance criteria: Zero level jumps greater than 1 on all public pages; no styling change.
resolution_note: FIXED. 20 pages -> 0. Changes: footer .ft__h h4->h3 (63 tags, 22 pages); .rpost/.tc2/.btl__c item titles h4->h3 (69 tags, 16 files) with blog/css/blog.css selectors updated to match; .rel-card h4->h3 (5 tags) with css/style.css selector updated; contact/ and partners/ section h3->h2; route-finder .rcard__dest h3->h2 (32 tags). Verified: 0 tag mismatches and 0 nested headings across 65 files; computed font-size/weight/colour identical before and after on every affected component; 0 stranded h4 site-wide.

issue: One WhatsApp link opened in the same tab and omitted rel=noopener.
evidence: Reproduced: 7 wa.me links on the homepage; the FAQ answer link had target=(none) rel=(none) while the other 6 had target=_blank rel=noopener.
affected visitor: Any visitor tapping the link from the FAQ
likely booking impact: Losing the visitor's place in the booking decision.
recommendation: Match the site convention.
acceptance criteria: All wa.me links have target=_blank and rel containing noopener.
resolution_note: FIXED. Added target=_blank rel="noopener noreferrer". Verified in the rendered DOM: 7 of 7 homepage WhatsApp links now carry target=_blank and rel=noopener.

issue: Only 1 of 7 homepage WhatsApp CTAs carried data-cta, making closing-CTA attribution unreliable.
evidence: Reproduced in the rendered DOM: 7 wa.me links, data-cta present on 1.
likely booking impact: Without per-CTA attribution the owner cannot tell which placement earns enquiries.
recommendation: Add data-cta to each homepage WhatsApp CTA.
acceptance criteria: Every wa.me CTA on the homepage carries data-cta.
resolution_note: FIXED. 6 static CTAs marked; the 7th is rendered by reviews-grid.js and already carried it. Verified rendered: 7 of 7 have data-cta. No new events introduced — conversion-tracking.js already fired on any wa.me href, so this changes attribution quality only.

issue: Two parallel event vocabularies describe the same clicks.
evidence: js/conversion-tracking.js emits whatsapp_click/call_click; js/main.js emits whatsapp_enquiry + whatsapp_booking (Ads AW-18103087307) and phone_click. Measured: one WhatsApp tap produces 3 dataLayer entries, one phone tap 2. Each NAME fires once, so nothing duplicates at dataLayer level.
likely booking impact: Double counting only if GA4 tags are built on both names for one action.
recommendation: Choose one vocabulary per action in GTM and document the authoritative one.
acceptance criteria: GTM contains exactly one tag per user action.
resolution_note: Blocked — requires GTM dashboard access, which is outside the repository.

issue: No link between a WhatsApp click and a confirmed booking.
evidence: GTM, GA4 (G-P3WJ9FXDF2) and Ads (AW-18103087307) all present and firing. whatsapp_click is the conversion signal; nothing records whether the enquiry became a trip.
likely booking impact: Optimising on clicks can grow unqualified enquiries while bookings stay flat.
recommendation: Add a short per-page booking reference to the WhatsApp prefill and log it on confirmation, or reconcile weekly.
acceptance criteria: A weekly enquiry count and confirmed-booking count exist for the same period.
resolution_note: Blocked — requires an operator process decision, not a code change.

issue: Fare overage terms are thin: waiting/extra-km 25% of pages, night charges 14%, driver allowance 15%, state tax 32%.
evidence: Topic scan across 59 public pages. 12 pages show fare figures without stating one-way vs round-trip alongside them.
likely booking impact: Unstated overage rules cause hesitation and end-of-trip disputes.
recommendation: Publish one fare-terms component wherever a fare appears.
acceptance criteria: Every page showing a fare also states per-car basis, one-way vs round-trip, and the rate beyond the included allowance.
resolution_note: Blocked on owner — requires actual km/hour allowances and overage rates.

issue: High-frequency superlatives and absolutes need substantiation or softening.
evidence: Claim catalogue built during implementation (distinct phrasings, not regex counts). TWO CORRECTIONS to the original audit: (1) the "guaranteed" family is almost entirely HONEST HEDGES — "We cannot guarantee an exact arrival time", "cannot guarantee specific birds" — these are good practice and were wrongly flagged; (2) the "best/#1/top-rated" count included innocuous phrases such as "best time to visit". Genuine remaining items: 24/7 (PST-07), "Verified Google Reviews" (40 pages), "no hidden/no surge" (22 phrasings), "within minutes" (23 phrasings, dominant "Usually replies within minutes" on 21 pages), "affordable" (21 pages, one shared footer line).
likely booking impact: Unsupported superlatives reduce credibility with the international segment.
recommendation: Review each family; keep what is evidenced, replace the rest with checkable statements.
acceptance criteria: Every remaining absolute claim is owner-confirmed or replaced.
resolution_note: PARTIALLY FIXED. Driver-verification claim resolved site-wide: docs/claims-policy-audit.md records that the owner already had "verified drivers" removed from index.html and about/ as unevidenced, but it survived on 7 blog pages and in the homepage hero. Applied the same already-approved treatment to all 8 ("verified local drivers" -> "local drivers who know these routes"; "a verified local driver" -> "a local driver who knows the route"). Verified: 0 driver-verification claims remain on public pages. All other families are service commitments or response-time promises and remain PENDING OWNER.

affected visitor: Homepage visitors — the largest single entry point

acceptance criteria: Homepage prefill uses the same structured field list as route pages.
